title: The Monkey and the Turtle
author: Philippine folk tale
source: Public domain. Retold in English from the classic Philippine folk tale, with a gentler ending.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One day, a monkey and a turtle were walking along the river when they found a banana tree floating in the water. They pulled it to the bank together.

segments.speaker: monkey
segments.text: "I found it first! But since you helped, we shall split it. I will take the top half — see how full of leaves it is!"

segments.speaker: turtle
segments.text: "Then I will take the bottom half, with the roots."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The monkey laughed at the turtle's poor bare half. He planted his leafy top in the ground, and the turtle planted her half with the roots. But leaves without roots soon wither — and roots know how to grow. Before long, the monkey's tree was brown and dry, while the turtle's tree grew tall and heavy with sweet golden bananas.

segments.speaker: turtle
segments.text: "Oh dear. My bananas are ripe, but my legs are too short to climb."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Along came the monkey, licking his lips.

segments.speaker: monkey
segments.text: "Dear friend! I am the finest climber in the forest. I shall pick your bananas for you — you may have every one that falls."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Up the trunk he scampered. But instead of dropping the bananas down, the greedy monkey sat in the branches and ate them, one after another after another.

segments.speaker: monkey
segments.text: "Mmm! Sweet! Delicious! Perhaps I shall leave you the peels!"

segments.speaker: turtle
segments.text: "Come down! Those are my bananas! I planted, I watered, I waited!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the monkey only laughed and kept eating.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the patient turtle thought of a clever trick. She gathered sharp coconut shells and set them all around the bottom of the tree, points up, like a little fence. Then she hid under a big leaf and called out in a spooky voice,

segments.speaker: turtle
segments.text: "Monkey! Monkey! The hunter is coming with his dogs!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The monkey was so frightened that he leapt from the tree without looking — and landed BOTTOM-FIRST right on the coconut shells!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He hopped and rubbed and hollered, and to this very day, that is why monkeys have hard, calloused bottoms — or so the old folks say.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The monkey, quite sore and quite ashamed, brought the turtle a whole armful of bananas the next morning to say sorry. The turtle shared them, because that is what she had wanted all along — a friend to share bananas with. And from then on, whenever they found a banana tree, the monkey climbed, the turtle counted, and both of them ate exactly half. But everyone in the forest agreed: the slow little turtle was the cleverest of them all.
